summary: Intermittent serial request hang when customers repeat identical completions (kvcatalog staleness)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that when issuing the same completion request back-to-back within the same session, a subset of requests hang for 3-10s (observed as ~p99) before returning a response. This appeared after a platform patch to the kvcatalog service rolled out to us-east on 2026-03-09.

Impact:
- BrightWrite production traffic experiences elevated p99 latency for repeat completions causing timeouts and user-facing slowdowns.
- Approximately 0.6% of repeat identical requests hit the issue during peak.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (customer reserved capacity) in us-east; running redwood-v2-medium for completions.
- Patch to kvcatalog v2.1.8 deployed 2026-03-09 02:12 UTC.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Open a session and send prompt A, get completion.
2) Immediately send the identical prompt A again (within 500ms to 2s).
3) Observe that the second request occasionally blocks ~3-10s before returning; other times it is normal (<200ms).

Logs and immediate observations:
- Support logs show the API request reached edge, routed to serving instance, and waiting on kvcatalog shard lookup.
- kvcatalog returned a 200 but with stale index_version header for affected requests.
- SRE metrics: kvcatalog read latency spikes correlate with hanging completions.

Customer provided artifacts:
- Raw request/response traces (trace IDs included below).
- SDK logs showing retry/backoff behavior.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:20 UTC - Support triage: confirmed reproducible on customer's workload; severity escalated to P1.
2026-03-10 10:05 UTC - SRE captured tail latencies on kvcatalog shards; high read variance on shard-17.

2026-03-10 11:12 UTC - Correlation found between kvcatalog index_version mismatch and serving runtime waiting for catalog refresh; repeated identical prompts hit a fast-path that assumes catalog freshness.

2026-03-10 13:40 UTC - Hypothesis: a race between kvcatalog background reindex job and cache invalidation led to temporary staleness flag; serving runtime serialized requests waiting for catalog refresh, amplifying p99 for repeated calls.

2026-03-11 02:30 UTC - Reproduced locally by running high-frequency repeat-request test harness against a snapshot of dedicated pool; observed same serial waiting behavior when index_version advanced mid-session.

2026-03-11 07:50 UTC - Added additional logging to serving-runtime to capture catalog_version per request; logs show requests that hang have catalog_version mismatch and enter a blocking refresh path.
2026-03-11 12:10 UTC - Engineering patch proposed: make refresh path non-blocking for in-flight identical requests and introduce optimistic fallback to previous index for up to 250ms.
2026-03-11 18:00 UTC - Temporary mitigation: rolled back kvcatalog reindex schedule for us-east dedicated pools and enabled a per-shard refresh backoff setting to reduce thrash.
comments: BrightWrite Support (2026-03-10 08:58 UTC): 'We've started seeing repeat completions stall intermittently after your most recent deploy; attaching traces and sample trace IDs: trace-20260310-01, trace-20260310-02.'
Alice Chen (Support) (2026-03-10 09:05 UTC): 'Thanks — triaging now. Can you confirm whether these requests are identical including metadata/final_tokens? Also which model and region?'
BrightWrite Engineer (2026-03-10 09:12 UTC): 'Confirmed identical payloads. Model: redwood-v2-medium. Region: us-east.'
Diego Morales (SRE) (2026-03-10 10:20 UTC): 'Captured kvcatalog read variance on shard-17 during the window. Adding shard-level logs and increasing sampling for hot paths.'

Samir Patel (Eng) (2026-03-11 13:05 UTC): 'Proposed non-blocking refresh patch: https://github.com/redwood/realtime-kv/pull/9876 — this will let serving runtime continue with prior index while refreshing in background for a short window.'

BrightWrite Support (2026-03-12 02:44 UTC): 'After the mitigation rollback, we saw a ~4x reduction in repeat-request p99 spikes during peak. Still seeing occasional outliers; will continue to monitor.'
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation: rolled back kvcatalog reindex schedule and adjusted per-shard refresh backoff (2026-03-11). Engineering patch (non-blocking refresh + optimistic fallback) landed in PR #9876 and is scheduled for canary on us-east dedicated pools 2026-03-14. Follow-up: monitor p99 for repeat identical requests for 72h; plan a full rollout only after canary validates a >90% reduction in observed hang rate. Postmortem to include tuning guidance for kvcatalog reindex cadence for dedicated pools.
